newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity closes down on long liquidation.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity closes down on long liquidation.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures settled lower Tuesday as long positions were liquidated, despite an early resurgence in spread trading for nearby contracts, market sources said.
"The July-August spreads were active, but a lot of selling came in during the afternoon. That drove prices back down," said one dealer.
Traders also said forecasts for below-normal temperatures in the U.S. West helped put downward pressure on futures prices.
July Palo Verde (PV) fell 81 cents to close at $26.82 per megawatt hour (MWh), compared with a high for the day of $27.50.
August PV fell $1.06 to settle at $29.74 and September dropped 42 cents to $26.90.
The July California-Oregon border (COB) contract fell 45 cents to close at $16.76 per MWh.
August COB fell 51 cents to $21.19 and September lost 45 cents to settle at $21.50.
"A lot of marketers got caught long. They weren't worried about prices, they were worried about size," said another trader.
NYMEX said as of 1535 EDT an estimated total of 828 COB and 750 PV contracts had traded.
Meanwhile, power generating units in the West were being returned to service from spring maintenance and refueling outages.

The 1,221 MW unit 2 at Palo Verde nuclear station in Arizona was operatng at 90 percent of capacity early Tuesday and was expected to reach 100 percent later today. The unit was curtailed Monday to repair a feedwater heater tube leak.

Southwest forecasts called for generally fair and dry conditions through Thursday with temperatures expected to be two to six degrees below normal. Clouds, showers and thunderstorms were possible across the region later in the week.
The Pacific Northwest was expected to see temperatures near to slightly below normal into the weekend, with scattered showers and thunderstorms during the period.
